name: Interventional Pain
tag: Procedure mix, ASC/equity, wRVUs, referral base, APP leverage, quality/risk, contract terms.
questions: What is the wRVU threshold and conversion factor?
Is the base guaranteed or a draw?
What procedures are supported now versus aspirational?

samples.name: Hospital-employed Pain Program
samples.pros: Stable system, benefits, local referral base, lower business risk.
samples.cons: Clarify autonomy, procedure mix, threshold, noncompete, and whether advanced procedures are truly supported.

samples.name: Orthopedic Group Pain Role
samples.pros: Strong referral stream, procedures, PM&R/ortho alignment, productivity upside.
samples.cons: Commute, noncompete, pressure for volume, and ASC/equity details need review.

samples.name: Private Practice with ASC Path
samples.pros: Highest upside if ASC/equity is real and referral volume is durable.
samples.cons: Buy-in risk, debt, valuation, restrictive covenant, and true distributions must be verified.

Compensation: Is the base salary guaranteed, or does it convert to a draw?
What is the wRVU threshold before bonus begins?
Is the wRVU rate paid only above threshold or on all wRVUs?
Is there any deficit carryforward, productivity clawback, or bonus cap?
How frequently are productivity bonuses calculated and paid?
Are sign-on, relocation, CME, student loan, retention, or call stipends available?
Are peer-to-peer denials, prior authorizations, and no-show procedure slots considered in productivity expectations?
ASC / ancillary / partnership: Is ASC ownership, partnership, or ancillary income available?
What is the buy-in amount, valuation method, financing option, and expected timeline?
What have historical ASC distributions been over the last 3 years?
What happens to ownership if the physician leaves, is terminated, or relocates?
Are imaging, DME, PT, lab, real estate, or management-company revenues included or excluded?
Are there restrictions on where procedures can be performed?
Who controls block time, case allocation, and payer contracting?
Clinical model: How many clinic days and procedure days are expected each week?
What percentage of the practice is medication management versus interventional care?
Are SCS, PNS, MILD, Intracept, kyphoplasty, pumps, and advanced procedures supported now?
Who controls procedure scheduling, referral triage, prior authorizations, and denial appeals?
What is the expected new-patient referral volume and current wait time?
Are fluoroscopy, ultrasound, sedation, nursing, and device-rep support available?
What is the opioid policy and who manages chronic medication refills?
APP supervision: Will NPs/PAs see pain patients under my supervision?
How many APPs would I supervise at full ramp?
Is APP supervision compensated separately? If so, how much per APP, per visit, per chart, or as a percentage of collections/RVUs?
Who owns liability, controlled-substance workflow, refills, inbox messages, and chart review?
Are APP encounters credited to the physician, the APP, or the group?
Can APP supervision be declined or renegotiated if workload becomes excessive?
Quality bonus: Is there a quality bonus separate from productivity?
Which metrics matter: access, patient satisfaction, opioid compliance, documentation, denial rate, procedure outcomes, complications, or referral leakage?
What is the maximum quality bonus and historical average payout?
Can metrics reduce compensation or only add upside?
Are targets formula-based, discretionary, or changed annually?
Lifestyle / support: What is call burden, after-hours phone expectation, and weekend coverage?
Is there protected admin time for notes, peer-to-peers, and prior authorizations?
How much travel between sites is expected?
Are scribes, MAs, nurses, authorization staff, and procedure schedulers adequate?
How often are procedure days lost to staffing, authorization, or payer denials?
Contract risk: What is the noncompete radius, duration, and specialty scope?
Is malpractice occurrence or claims-made, and who pays tail?
Are sign-on, relocation, CME, loan repayment, or bonus payments subject to repayment?
Can my CV be submitted only with written authorization?
Who owns patient lists, referral relationships, and procedure-center access if I leave?

Clinical Fit: Procedure mix matches current skillset and future growth goals.
Medication-management burden is acceptable and supported by policy.
ASC/fluoro/sedation/device infrastructure is real, staffed, and available.
Compensation Upside: Base, wRVU threshold, conversion factor, ASC/equity, and APP supervision are all quantified.
Advanced procedures and denials do not make productivity targets unrealistic.
Lifestyle Fit: Clinic/procedure split, prior-auth burden, call, and travel fit family life.
Risk Safety: Noncompete, CV submission control, tail, ASC buy-in, and clawbacks are acceptable.
Strategic Fit: Referral network, local reputation, and procedure platform improve long-term market value.
Collaborative Fit: Ortho, neurosurgery, PM&R, PT, psychology, and primary care referrals are aligned.
